title: ServiceEvent
description: A single compliance-relevant action performed on an EnsembleElement: inspection, cleaning, repair, retirement, or disposition. Discriminated by event_type. See 01-nfpa-1850-clause-mapping.md for the compliance rationale behind each field.

event_id.description: Globally unique event identifier, e.g. a UUID.

performed_by_org_id.description: FK to Organization.org_id — the department, ISP, or manufacturer that performed this event.

performed_by_person_id.description: FK to Person.person_id — who carried out the action (inspector, technician, etc.). Null when performed by an ISP without person-level tracking.

issued_to_person_id.description: NFPA 1851 4.3.3(1)-(2). Used only when event_type = ISSUANCE: the recipient of the element, distinct from performed_by_person_id (who conducted the issuance transaction, if tracked separately). Null for all other event types.

location.description: Free-text or facility identifier for where the event took place.

defect_codes.description: Suggested values documented in defect-code.yaml, but NOT a closed enum — any string is valid. Unlike NFIRS's approach of enumerating a code for every possible scenario, PPE-REX keeps this open: common values are documented for consistency, but a defect that doesn't fit the list should just be described in notes rather than forced into OTHER plus a workaround.

method.description: Free-text cleaning/inspection method, relevant mainly for ADVANCED_CLEANING, DISINFECTION_SANITIZATION, and SPECIALIZED_CLEANING events. Deliberately not a closed enum — cleaning technology is evolving (e.g., CO2 cleaning is an increasingly common specialized-cleaning method) and a fixed vocabulary would need constant revision to stay current.

attachments.description: Supporting evidence: photos, lab reports, cleaning-verification data (wash temp, detergent, water hardness), etc.

hash.description: SHA-256 hash of the attachment content, for tamper-evidence.

trigger.description: What caused this event to happen. Carries the optional NERIS linkage.

reason.description: NFPA 1851 4.3.3(8): the reason for the action, distinct from trigger_type's structured category. Required in practice for ADVANCED_CLEANING, DISINFECTION_SANITIZATION, and SPECIALIZED_CLEANING events even though not schema-enforced as required, since 4.3.3(8) explicitly calls for a documented reason.

neris_incident_id.description: Reference to a NERIS incident ID, when trigger_type = EXPOSURE_INCIDENT and the department has correlated this event to a specific incident.

related_event_id.description: FK to another ServiceEvent.event_id, e.g. the failed routine inspection that triggered this advanced inspection.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 hash of this event's canonical content, computed at finalization.
